idiom_name: client-side delegate object + lookup abstraction + remote service interface
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define a local interface containing exactly the coarse-grained operations the client needs, then inject an implementation that (1) resolves the service through a lookup or configuration abstraction rather than embedding naming details, (2) owns the transport reference and any bounded, invalidatable handle cache privately, (3) invokes the remote operation with an explicit deadline or cancellation policy and (4) translates transport/naming failures into application-level errors while chaining the cause and preserving retryability. Keep the delegate thin—lookup, invocation, translation and remote policy only, never business rules—and guard the cache so concurrent callers cannot race; re-resolve on stale-handle failures instead of caching forever. Two delegation strategies from Core J2EE remain useful: Delegate Proxy forwards compatible calls to the service, while Delegate Adapter transforms heterogeneous contracts such as XML B2B payloads. Pair the delegate one-to-one with a Session Facade on the service side when workflow aggregation belongs there; with modern DI, do not add a class whose only job is to rename a generated client.
pitfalls: Mirror every remote method -> the delegate becomes a second API surface that changes with every service release -> expose only the coarse-grained operations this client actually needs.
Cache a remote handle forever -> failover, redeploy or session expiry leaves callers stuck on a dead target -> bound the lifetime, invalidate on stale-handle errors and re-resolve.

Translate failures without the original cause or status -> retryability and diagnostics disappear behind a generic application error -> chain the cause and preserve retryable-versus-fatal information.

Retry every failure automatically -> an ambiguous timeout can duplicate a non-idempotent write and amplify an outage -> retry only classified idempotent operations with bounded backoff and visible exhaustion.

Copy per-request credentials or deadlines into shared delegate state -> concurrent tenants can observe one another's context -> pass request-scoped metadata explicitly or use a correctly scoped client.

Keep hand-written delegates after DI arrived -> every lookup is already hidden by injection and the wrapper is ceremony nobody maintains -> add a delegate only where domain mapping, batching or remote policy remains.

Let each per-client delegate own shared business rules -> the same entitlement and authorization logic duplicates and diverges across every delegate, as it did across SoundCloud's BFFs -> move shared capabilities into a server-side service and keep delegates to access and translation.

Assume hiding the lookup makes calls cheap -> callers loop over fine-grained operations and each iteration pays a network round trip -> measure round trips and batch behind coarse delegate operations instead of adding another layer.
